inputs.root_cause: FF6-EVENT-000291 built and proved a pattern for nrrd: validate() accepting a raw source (bytes/path/stream) directly, catching load-time errors and returning a FATAL Diagnostic instead of an uncaught exception. FF6-EVENT-000292's own audit found safetensors/ipynb already had this; xliff and ubl did not -- both validate() functions accepted only an already-loaded document, with zero try/except. Not tied to a specific unresolved obligation for either format, but a real, tested robustness/API-consistency improvement.
inputs.obligation_targeted: None directly -- general capability generalization across xliff and ubl's own validate() API surface, matching the now-consistent contract nrrd/safetensors/ipynb all share.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 8 new tests (4 per format) proving: malformed bytes report a FATAL diagnostic not a raise; a nonexistent path reports a FATAL diagnostic not a raise; a valid source produces an identical report whether given as a path, raw bytes, or a preloaded document.
inputs.regression_tier: full xliff and ubl suites plus 6-format regression, mypy --strict, ruff

execution_steps: 1. Confirmed all four other formats' own validate() dispatch behavior directly (not assumed): safetensors already accepts SafeTensorsDocument | bytes | bytearray | memoryview | str and catches all exceptions; ipynb already accepts IpynbDocument | Mapping | Source and catches ResourceLimitError/IpynbError/OSError/TypeError/ValueError. Both already correct, no gap.

2. Confirmed xliff's validate(value: XliffDocument, ...) and ubl's validate(value: UblDocument, ...) both accept only an already-loaded document with zero raw-source path and zero try/except -- the identical structural gap nrrd had before FF6-EVENT-000291.

3. Checked both packages' own load()/errors.py: XliffError/UblError are each the shared base exception class for their own parse/validation errors, and load() is exported from each package's own codec/__init__.py with no import-cycle risk into the validation module.

4. Extended both validate() functions identically: value: XxxDocument -> value: XxxDocument | BinarySource; when not already a Document, call load(value, limits=limits) and catch (XliffError / UblError), returning a FATAL '{fmt}.source.unreadable' Diagnostic instead of propagating.

5. Verified with standalone repros before writing tests: malformed bytes, a nonexistent path, and (critically) that a VALID source produces byte-identical diagnostics whether passed as a path, raw bytes, or an already-loaded document -- confirming the new dispatch path doesn't silently diverge from the existing one.

6. Added tests/python/xliff/test_xliff_validate_raw_source.py and tests/python/ubl/test_ubl_validate_raw_source.py (4 tests each, same shape, not tied to any existing obligation-named test file since neither obligation set names this specific gap).

7. Ran mypy --strict (clean, both files), ruff (clean, both files), the two full package suites (xliff 543 unchanged since dispatch doesn't affect existing document-value callers; ubl 1018 unchanged), and the 6-format regression (3640 -> 3648 passed, +8 exactly matching new tests, 0 failed).
